statement: The service shall help companies prove their eligibility for public procurement across borders without repeatedly gathering and resubmitting the same evidence.
The service shall make it easier to identify what evidence is needed.
The service shall get evidence validated.
The service shall bundle evidence into a dossier.
The service shall send the dossier to the right authority in a usable form.
The service shall support end-to-end use by economic operators.
The service shall support end-to-end use by contracting authorities.
The service shall interact with public sector or registry systems that issue and validate attestations.
The service shall support a support or administrative role for managing mappings, translation rules, and service configuration.
The service shall allow economic operators to track missing or expired items so they can complete the dossier correctly.
The service shall authenticate incoming dossiers for contracting authorities.
The backend shall support mapping national criteria and evidence types to the shared European requirements.
The Virtual Company Dossier service shall handle the relevant EU and national languages involved in each procurement case.
The original attestation in the evidence and dossier package shall remain intact.
The interview scope shall focus on the Virtual Company Dossier service.
The Virtual Company Dossier service shall support businesses in identifying evidence.
The Virtual Company Dossier service shall support businesses in validating evidence.
The Virtual Company Dossier service shall support authorities in receiving evidence across borders.
The service should make the cross-border dossier process workable in practice.
The current process is mostly fragmented and manual.
The current process varies significantly by country.
Businesses must determine the required evidence themselves.
Businesses must contact different national registers or issuing bodies to obtain evidence.
Businesses must collect documents in separate formats.
Businesses must compile collected documents into a package and submit it through the channel accepted by the authority.
Businesses often must perform extra translation or reformatting work.
Authorities receive and check evidence dossiers inconsistently.
Authorities may receive documents in different languages and structures.
Authorities often must verify authenticity manually.
Authorities often must manually map local evidence to their own procurement criteria.
There is not yet a harmonized cross-border process that everyone relies on.
The service shall minimize manual back-and-forth.
The service shall reduce manual back-and-forth related to finding the right evidence and proving that the evidence is valid.
The service shall help an operator identify exactly what evidence is needed for a procurement.
The service shall allow an operator to retrieve or reference evidence from trusted sources.
The service shall package evidence so that authorities can read and trust it without re-entering the information.
The service shall support smoother reception and interpretation of the dossier on the authority side.
The service shall provide translation where needed for dossier reception and interpretation.
The service shall provide a clearer mapping between national criteria and shared European requirements.
The service shall make cross-border procurement faster.
The service shall make cross-border procurement more consistent.
The service shall make cross-border procurement less burdensome for both sides.
The system shall provide tracking and status visibility.
The system shall allow the operator to see what evidence has been found.
The system shall provide traceability.
The system shall allow the authority to see where the evidence came from and when it was issued or checked.
The system shall support reuse of valid evidence or attestations in later dossiers.
The system should provide automated alerts to the operator before an attestation expires.
The system should provide automated alerts to the operator when something is rejected during validation.
The system should support automated notifications or reminders for missing, expiring, or invalid evidence as part of the tracking and reuse features.
The tracking and reuse features should help keep dossiers current and reduce the risk of incomplete applications.
The system shall include access control and authentication.
The system shall provide strong identity handling before operators can create dossiers.
For the first version of the service, the system shall identify required evidence.
The system shall present evidence information in a way that a business can act on without having to interpret each national rule manually.
The evidence list should be quite detailed.
The evidence list should include the document or attestation type.
The evidence list should include the issuing body or source if that is known.
The evidence list should include the validity period or expiry rules.
The evidence list should include any format requirements for submission.
The evidence list should show whether the evidence can be reused from an existing dossier or must be freshly obtained.
For the first version, the system shall use automatic derivation of evidence requirements from tender data as the default approach.
For the first version, the system shall allow users to manually adjust evidence requirements as a fallback.
The system shall allow users to correct evidence requirements when the system misses something.
The system shall allow users to add evidence requirements when the system misses something.
The system shall not block users if the automated mapping is not perfect.
The service shall fetch the evidence from the source when the source supports direct retrieval.
When direct retrieval is not possible, the service shall create a trusted reference or link and capture enough metadata to prove the evidence source and the time it was checked.
The system shall ensure that the authority can trust the evidence as originating from an official source.
The system shall consider official public registers as trusted sources.
The system shall consider competent authorities as trusted sources.
The system shall consider other government-backed evidence providers as trusted sources.
The system shall consider accredited organizations as trusted sources when they are the recognized issuer for a specific attestation.
The system shall treat self-declared or commercially repackaged sources as untrusted unless a formal trust framework exists behind them.
The service shall confirm that an attestation is authentic before it is added to the dossier.
The service shall confirm that an attestation is current before it is added to the dossier.
The service shall confirm that an attestation matches the required criterion before it is added to the dossier.
The service shall validate issuer validity as part of attestation checking.
The service shall validate expiration as part of attestation checking.
The service shall validate the integrity of the document or payload as part of attestation checking.
The service shall determine whether evidence is still acceptable for the procurement as part of attestation checking.
The system shall handle evidence validation failures differently depending on the type of failure.
The system shall block evidence from submission if it is clearly invalid, expired, or cannot be trusted at all.
The system shall issue a warning for softer evidence issues such as a minor metadata mismatch or an uncertain mapping.
The system shall allow the user to review evidence after a warning and decide whether to proceed.
The system shall permit submission only of acceptable evidence.
The service shall include whatever cover metadata is needed for routing, identification, and audit trail.
The system shall provide confirmation that the package was delivered successfully upon submission.
The system shall provide a receipt or transaction reference if the authority supports that.
If submission fails, the system shall provide a clear error so the user knows whether to retry or fix the package first.
The authority side shall verify that the received package is complete and readable.
The system shall consider the constraints of national registers or issuing bodies that provide evidence, because those constraints determine what can be fetched and validated.
The system shall involve legal and compliance stakeholders because cross-border trust rules, evidence retention rules, and translation rules are sensitive.

The system shall consider the technical needs of PEPPOL operators or integration providers, if they are part of the chain, because those needs affect how practical the service is to deploy and support.
The system shall prioritize accessibility and usability.
The first version of the system shall have a very guided and forgiving flow.
The system shall be designed with interoperability in mind from the start.
The first version shall work well in a normal browser without special software.
Companies bidding for public contracts across borders must gather the same kinds of proof repeatedly from different national registers and authorities.
The rules and formats for the required evidence are not harmonized.
The service shall help companies identify what evidence is needed.
The service shall help companies collect the required evidence.
The service shall help companies validate the required evidence.
The service shall package the evidence into a dossier that a contracting authority in another country can trust and understand.
The system shall make it easier for contracting authorities to receive a standard dossier.
The system shall allow contracting authorities to check the dossier against the relevant procurement criteria.
The system shall allow contracting authorities to view the dossier even when the original evidence comes from different national sources and languages.
The system shall reduce the time and effort required for economic operators to prove eligibility.
The system shall eliminate the need for economic operators to manually chase certificates and resubmit the same information for every tender.
The system shall provide economic operators with a smooth experience for viewing the required information.
The system shall provide economic operators with validated evidence.
The system shall allow economic operators to assemble a dossier with minimal friction.
The system shall provide contracting authorities with a dossier they can trust.
The system shall enable contracting authorities to quickly verify the dossier.
The system shall enable contracting authorities to review the dossier in a consistent way.
The system shall support translation or mapping of underlying evidence from another country to local criteria when needed.
The system should reduce the time required to prepare and submit a compliant dossier.
The system should reduce rejected or incomplete submissions.
The system should guide users to the correct evidence before submission.
The system should validate evidence before submission.
The system should enable faster review on the authority side.
The system should reduce manual follow-up requests on the authority side.
The main user on the economic operator side is usually someone preparing the tender submission.
The economic operator side may include a bid manager, compliance officer, or legal administrator as the main user.
The economic operator user shall search for the required evidence.
The economic operator user shall request or import attestations.
The economic operator user shall check validity.
The economic operator user shall compile the dossier package for submission.
On the contracting authority side, the typical user is a procurement officer or evaluator.
The contracting authority user shall authenticate the package.
The contracting authority user shall review the contents of the package.
The contracting authority user shall check whether the package satisfies the procurement criteria.
There may also be technical or registry service roles behind the scenes.
The economic operator shall identify the evidence needed and retrieve it from its records or request it from the relevant source.
The system shall support handoff of a dossier package through the platform to the contracting authority after the attestations are validated.
The contracting authority shall receive the dossier package.
The contracting authority shall be able to translate or map the evidence to local criteria.
The contracting authority shall review the dossier package for procurement assessment.
The system shall support a back-and-forth request for clarification when something is missing or unclear.
The system shall operate within the PEPPOL ecosystem.
The system shall rely on existing interoperability patterns rather than inventing a new proprietary exchange model.
The system shall fit European public procurement rules.
The system shall fit cross-border evidence rules.
The system shall include national registers as part of its legal and evidentiary context.
The system shall include attestation sources as part of its legal and evidentiary context.
The system shall integrate with existing identity capabilities where available.
The system shall integrate with existing authentication capabilities where available.
The system shall integrate with existing translation capabilities where available.
The system shall cope with external sources that expose data in different formats.
The system shall cope with external sources that have different availability levels.
The system shall cope with different national rules.
The system shall cope with different APIs.
The system shall cope with different trust levels.
For an economic operator, an attestation is usually a proof document or trusted statement that they need to obtain and include.
For an economic operator, the dossier is the complete package they submit to demonstrate eligibility.
For a contracting authority, the dossier is an evidence bundle to assess.
For a contracting authority, an attestation is one of the source items that supports a claim.
Terminology may vary by country.
A shared glossary would probably be important.
The system shall explain what each item means in the local context and whether it is accepted for the intended procurement.
The system shall make translation-related issues explicit before submission.
The system shall make validity period information explicit before submission.
The system shall make it explicit before submission whether a document is official enough.
Users may not treat the terms “evidence,” “certificate,” “declaration,” “proof,” and “exclusion grounds” as interchangeable.
An economic operator may consider a declaration sufficient when a contracting authority expects a formal certificate or a digitally signed attestation.
Terms related to validity, authenticity, and equivalence are especially sensitive.
A document that is acceptable in one jurisdiction may only be considered equivalent in another jurisdiction.
The system should explain relationships among validity, authenticity, and equivalence very carefully.
The system shall flag missing evidence, expired attestations, invalid attestations, translation gaps, and mismatches between the original document and the required shared criteria early.
The system shall explain exactly what is wrong in plain language.
The system shall point the operator to the next action instead of simply rejecting the dossier outright.
The system shall record the reason consistently when an authority cannot accept something.
The system shall allow the operator to correct and resubmit the dossier without losing the rest of the package.

The system shall detect when a submitted registry extract or local certificate is not sufficient because the authority requires a more specific attestation tied to a particular exclusion or selection criterion.
The system shall detect when a document is technically valid but too old.
The system shall detect when a translated document does not preserve the legal meaning expected by the authority.
The system shall compare the evidence against the target criterion before submission.
The system shall clearly show any gaps or equivalence issues before submission.
The system shall ideally suggest the exact missing attestation if one is needed.
The system shall ideally suggest a safer alternative if one exists.
The system shall support a controlled clarification loop.
The system shall allow the authority to flag an issue.
The system shall allow the authority to request a specific correction.
The system shall keep a clear record of what changed and why.
The system shall allow the operator to respond by replacing only the affected evidence or uploading an additional attestation.
The system shall support responding without rebuilding the whole dossier from scratch.
The exchange shall be timestamped and traceable.
The system shall make the comparison step very explicit and act as a pre-check.
The system shall map each required criterion to the evidence provided.
The system shall show a clear status for each criterion, such as satisfied, partially satisfied, missing, or doubtful equivalence.
An attestation should usually be created outside the system by the issuing body or imported from a trusted source.
The dossier should be updated whenever an attestation is replaced or a criterion changes.
After completion, the package and its audit trail should be retained for a defined legal period.
The system shall preserve visibility into what the operator had at the time of submission and what was later corrected.
The records shall include enough detail to prove the chain of custody and the exact evidence used.
The records shall not expose unnecessary personal or commercial information beyond what each role is allowed to see.
The retention period may vary by country and case type.
The system shall support controlled archiving after the retention period ends.
The system shall make archived records no longer active.
The system shall allow archived records to be retrieved for audits, disputes, or legal reviews if needed.
The system shall allow deletion or anonymization only after the retention period has fully expired and no legal hold exists.
When deletion or anonymization is performed, the system shall preserve minimal metadata if that is allowed and useful for traceability.
The system should provide very guided onboarding for users.
The system should provide context-sensitive help.
The system should provide examples or templates to help reduce mistakes.
The system shall adapt its guidance over time based on user experience.
The system shall provide very detailed guidance to first-time users.
After a user has completed several dossiers successfully, the system shall reduce prompts and offer a more streamlined workflow.
The system shall keep help available on demand even when guidance is reduced.
The system shall allow administrators to see where users are struggling.
The system shall show administrators repeated validation errors and abandoned submissions as indicators of user struggle.
The system shall support improving training or guidance based on administrator insight into user struggle.
For new or infrequent operators, the system shall provide a step-by-step wizard that starts from the procurement notice.
The step-by-step wizard shall tell users exactly what evidence is needed and why.
The system shall display very plain status labels.
The system shall provide tooltips.
The system shall provide a review-before-submit screen.
The system shall capture the time spent on each step.
The system shall capture abandonment points.
The system shall capture how often users open help content or request clarification.
Administrators shall be able to see patterns by procedure.
Administrators shall be able to see patterns by country.
Administrators shall be able to see patterns by user segment.
The system shall handle the information carefully so that it supports improvement without turning into intrusive monitoring of individual users.
The system shall provide clear status indicators for evidence items that show whether each item is accepted, pending, rejected, or expired.
The system should provide a searchable help area or FAQ.
Performance is very important.
The system should perform well near tender deadlines when many users may be active at once.
Most screen actions, searches, and status checks should feel close to immediate.
For bigger operations such as compiling or translating a dossier, a short wait is acceptable.
The platform shall scale horizontally to cope with many dossiers.
The platform shall handle evidence lookups and submissions at the same time without slowing down.
The platform shall be designed to handle peak demand around major tender deadlines as a likely bottleneck.
The platform shall be designed to handle cross-border translation and validation traffic as a likely bottleneck.
The platform shall stay stable even if one national source or one external service is slow.
The platform shall allow users to continue where possible when a national source or external service is slow.
When a registry is unavailable, the system shall clearly indicate whether the problem is temporary and whether the user can retry later or continue with other parts of the dossier.
The system shall explicitly mark partial data so that it is not mistaken for a completed validation.
The dossier shall remain in a visible exception or pending state until the missing evidence is resolved.
The system shall provide source information to help maintain trust.
The system shall automatically retry transient failures.
The system shall limit automatic retries to sensible limits so it does not keep hammering a struggling registry.
If approved fallback sources are available, the platform shall use them.
The platform shall make it obvious which source was used.
The platform shall make it obvious whether the result is provisional or fully verified.
The system shall allow the user to keep working on other parts of the dossier while the blocked check remains queued in the background.
Validation requests shall be queued according to urgency and user impact.
Validation requests that block submission shall have higher priority than background checks or non-critical refreshes.
The system shall use separate queues or workers for different evidence types.
The system shall notify users when a stalled check resumes or completes.
The system shall provide a short explanation for why evidence items are not complete yet.
The system shall show when the evidence was last checked.
The system shall notify the user without requiring manual checking for status updates.
The notification message shall indicate whether the evidence item is now verified or still partially blocked.
The notification style shall be calm and factual.
The notification style shall resemble a system update rather than an alert unless the issue is still preventing submission.
The dossier view shall show a very clear status for each item.
The system shall provide a simple audit trail with the response time for each verification request.
The system shall provide a simple audit trail with any failure reason for each verification request.
Evidence shall be accepted when it fully matches the required criteria, comes from a trusted source, and receives a successful validation result.
Evidence shall be partially accepted when it is relevant but incomplete.
Evidence shall be partially accepted when it is stale.
Evidence shall be partially accepted when only some checks have passed.
Evidence shall be rejected when it clearly fails the rule or cannot be verified at all.
The system shall be strict on core legal requirements.
The system shall use review rather than automatic rejection when evidence is close enough but there is ambiguity in mapping between national and common European criteria.
Migration to the Virtual Company Dossier should be gradual rather than a big-bang switch.
Organizations will already have documents, internal registers, and local workflows in place before migration.
The migration process must handle inconsistent data quality.
The migration process must integrate with national systems that may not expose the same interfaces or semantics.
The system should support importing existing evidence.
The system should provide clear guidance on what still needs to be refreshed or reissued.
Legacy attestations may use different structures, terminology, and validity rules, which can prevent the system from mapping them cleanly into standardized dossier fields.
The conversion process may lose context such as the original issuer, scope, or expiry conditions.
Loss of context during conversion would affect legal meaning and user confidence.
The system should record exactly what was transformed.
Change management is the biggest challenge during gradual adoption of the Virtual Company Dossier.
Users must trust a new process while continuing to do business using the old process in parallel during the transition.
There is uncertainty about which evidence can be reused across borders without extra validation.
The system shall support an assessment phase in which the organization reviews existing evidence and determines what can realistically be mapped into the new dossier model.
The system shall support a parallel-run period in which users can compare old and new outputs before fully switching over.
The rollout should be conducted country by country or capability by capability.
The rollout strategy should account for member states being at different levels of readiness.
A national system should switch only when its mappings are proven stable.
The system shall support a discovery and mapping phase.
During the discovery and mapping phase, the organization shall identify its current evidence sources and gaps against the common dossier requirements.
The system shall support a pilot or parallel-run phase in which users test real cases without fully abandoning the legacy process.
When a company in one EU country bids for a public tender in another country, the system shall support proving the supplier's legal status.
When a company in one EU country bids for a public tender in another country, the system shall support proving the supplier's tax compliance.
When a company in one EU country bids for a public tender in another country, the system shall support proving the supplier's financial standing.
When a company in one EU country bids for a public tender in another country, the system shall support proving the supplier's professional qualifications.
The system shall support using evidence issued in the supplier's home country and accepted in the country of the tender.
The proof process shall support a fast and trusted way to compile and submit evidence.
The proof process shall allow the supplier to participate without repeating the same checks country by country.
The system shall represent eligibility evidence as demonstrating that the economic operator meets the eligibility and selection criteria for the specific procurement.
The system shall represent eligibility evidence as convincing the contracting authority that the supplier is allowed to bid.
The system shall represent eligibility evidence as convincing the contracting authority that the supplier is not excluded for legal reasons.
The system shall represent eligibility evidence as convincing the contracting authority that the supplier is not excluded for financial reasons.
The system shall represent eligibility evidence as convincing the contracting authority that the supplier is not excluded for technical reasons.
The system shall align with the PEPPOL framework and the applicable EU procurement and electronic identification rules.
The dossier exchange shall be interoperable and trustworthy across member states.
The dossier and attached evidence shall be packaged in a standardized way.
The system shall provide reliable authentication and validation.
The authority side shall be able to receive and open the dossier even when the documents come from another country.
The preparation process shall map national evidence types and criteria to the shared European requirements before submission.
Each country shall not interpret the documents on its own.
Evidence for cross-border dossiers often comes from different national registers or authorities.
Those evidence sources can have different formats.
Those evidence sources can have different languages.
Those evidence sources can have different delivery times.
The process must handle evidence expiry dates.
The process must include validity checks.
The process must handle missing attestations.
The process must handle attestations that need to be translated before submission.
The work must be organized as a guided workflow with validation steps.
The work must include reminders.
The work must include enough traceability for the supplier to see what is complete and what still needs attention before the dossier is sent.
The submission process shall not assume that a single successful send is sufficient to complete the dossier exchange.
When the dossier exchange service is down or delivery is uncertain, the system shall keep the dossier in a pending state.
When the dossier exchange service is down or delivery is uncertain, the system shall show the supplier that the dossier has not been accepted yet.
When the dossier exchange service is down or delivery is uncertain, the system shall retry or resume submission without losing the evidence package.
The process shall require a clear received confirmation from the authority before it is considered complete.
The system shall prevent the dossier from being treated as not submitted due to missing confirmation, to avoid deadline risk.
The system shall provide a pending state for dossier submissions to support reliability.
The system shall retry failed dossier submissions to support reliability.
The system shall treat a dossier as officially received only after the authority has acknowledged it.
The system shall avoid creating ambiguity about deadlines and legal acceptance.
The system shall define how long it retries failed submissions before failing fast and instructing the supplier to intervene manually.
The system shall balance automation so that it does not hide problems or make the process too fragile.
The service shall help the supplier identify the needed evidence.
The service shall allow the supplier to collect or upload the needed evidence.
The service shall validate that the dossier is complete enough to submit.
The service shall package the dossier.
The service shall transmit the dossier securely.
The service shall track dossier delivery status.
The service shall support pending, failed, and acknowledged delivery status states.
The service provider's responsibility shall end when the authority has received and acknowledged the dossier.
The service shall provide traceability and status history so the supplier can prove what happened in the event of a dispute.
The service shall keep some activities outside the core service boundary.
The service shall not assess the procurement case itself or decide whether the supplier should win the tender.
The service shall not fully take over manual follow-up with external authorities when a certificate is delayed or disputed.
The actual business decision shall remain with the supplier or the competent authority.
The bid or tender manager shall coordinate the whole dossier and ensure deadlines are met.
A compliance or legal person shall check that the evidence is acceptable.
A person from operations or finance shall provide the underlying documents and attestations.
The system shall support an administrator role for managing the organization, users, and access rights.
The system shall support an auditor or read-only reviewer role for internal oversight.
The system shall support a substitute or delegate role that can act when the main coordinator is absent.
The authority shall first confirm that it has received a usable package before proceeding with review.
If translated or mapped documents are available, the reviewer shall use them to verify compliance against the local criteria.
A legal or specialist reviewer may be brought in when something is unclear or exceptional.
In day-to-day work, people usually refer to individual items as evidence, certificate, or supporting document.
In day-to-day work, people usually refer to the full submission as a dossier or package.
Attestation is considered more formal than a normal document.
People often use the terms requirements, criteria, or conditions for both the national and European sets of requirements.
A national document may name a specific certificate or legal basis that does not exist in the same form elsewhere.
Country-specific variations exist in procurement eligibility rules.
Country-specific variations can affect the thresholds that trigger extra documents.
Each country can require its own certificates.
Each country can require its own registers.
Each country can require its own declarations.
The system shall show the relevant eligibility criteria and the evidence expected for those criteria after the user selects a procurement opportunity or authority to apply to.
The system shall provide very clear guidance to users.
The system shall support saved profiles.
The system shall account for rules that differ by country or procedure.
The system shall support unfamiliar languages encountered by users.
The service shall show the exact criterion the document is meant to satisfy.
The service shall show the issuing country or authority.
The service shall show the validity period.
The service shall show any special acceptance rules for that tender.
The service shall indicate whether a scanned copy is acceptable.
The service shall indicate whether a signed original is acceptable.
The service shall indicate whether an electronic attestation is acceptable.
If there is any ambiguity, the service shall indicate that the document is only provisionally acceptable or needs manual review.
A dossier shall not remain approved indefinitely after criteria changes.
If a change affects a core eligibility condition, the service may need to warn that the overall dossier is not submit-ready until that item is fixed.
The service shall accept evidence as-is only if it comes from a trusted source and exactly meets the tender’s format and validity rules.
If the evidence content is correct but its language or structure differs, the service shall translate or normalize it into the common dossier format.
The service shall keep the original proof attached for traceability when evidence is translated or normalized.
The service shall reject evidence that is too old, incomplete, or delivered through an untrusted channel.
When evidence is rejected, the service shall tell the operator to obtain a fresh document from the proper authority.
The service shall respond within a few seconds.
The system shall check for mismatched evidence before submission.
The service shall avoid forcing the operator to wait through long manual verification unless something is genuinely unclear.
For anything that is not fully certain, the service shall queue deeper checks in the background.
The system shall allow operators to see at a glance which dossier package version is current.
The system shall allow operators to see at a glance which dossier package version was submitted.
The system shall allow operators to see at a glance which earlier dossier package versions are archived for traceability.
If a dossier package is updated after validation or submission, the system shall mark the newer version as replacing the previous one.
If a change affects the contents of the submitted evidence or the eligibility status, the new version shall replace the old version as the active dossier.
If a change is only a non-material update, such as a metadata correction or translation improvement, it may remain alongside the previous record without invalidating it.
The determining rule shall be whether the change would alter what the contracting authority is relying on.

The system shall specially handle core eligibility evidence, including company registration, tax and social security status, insolvency or bankruptcy checks, and nationally issued professional or technical certificates.
The system shall map each core eligibility evidence item to the tender country’s required criterion.
The system shall treat a core eligibility evidence item as valid only if the issuing authority is recognized.
The system shall treat a core eligibility evidence item as valid only if the document is current for that opportunity.
The system shall treat a core eligibility evidence item as valid only if it satisfies the tender’s stated format and language rules.
If a national document does not directly match the tender requirement, the system shall show the closest acceptable equivalent and flag any gaps or extra checks needed.
The system shall leave special cross-border evidence exceptions undecided for the moment.
The system shall treat the described cross-border cases as sufficient to cover the main cross-border cases.
The system shall allow special exceptions to be revisited if they appear in later requirements or in a specific tender scenario.
While the transmission is still in progress, the delivery status shall remain "sending" or "pending delivery" so the operator knows it has not been completed yet.
If the transmission fails and a reason is available, the delivery status shall include the reason.
If no acknowledgment is received within the expected window, the system shall allow a "timed out" or "unknown" status.
Every dossier package shall include the operator identity.
The system shall include actual attested documents in a dossier package whenever the tender requires proof for the relevant criterion.
Supporting documents such as translations shall be optional unless the specific tender rules require them.
The system shall not force an evidence type into the package when the opportunity has no requirement for that evidence type.
Users shall be clearly notified that the package was assembled successfully but the delivery outcome is unresolved.
The follow-up action may be to retry the send.
If a revision changes anything that affects eligibility, evidence content, or the submitted package itself, the new version shall replace the previous version as the current official record.
The current evidence-handling approach is too fragmented across countries.
The current evidence-handling approach is too manual for businesses trying to reuse evidence in different tenders.
The new process shall let users find the right requirements faster.
The new process shall reuse already validated attestations where possible.
The new process shall package information in a way that contracting authorities can understand without having to chase extra paperwork.
The service shall be designed to handle fairly uneven demand.
The service shall handle peaks around major procurement deadlines and bursts from cross-border opportunities in a few high-use countries.
The service shall be able to handle many dossiers and users in parallel.
The maximum volume and maximum number of countries supported by the service are not yet defined and must be confirmed with the operational team.
The supplier should be able to correct or replace the evidence when a certificate is delayed, disputed, or incomplete.
The authority should keep the request pending until the issue is settled when a certificate is delayed, disputed, or incomplete.
Background checks shall continue when the provisional status is caused only by a temporary dependency, such as waiting for an external register response or a delayed validation service.

Background checks shall be stopped or revisited later if the source evidence changes, the user withdraws the dossier, or the checking result would no longer be trustworthy because the underlying data has been superseded.
The system shall stop retrying an exchange when the failure is clearly not temporary.
The system shall stop retrying an exchange for validation rejections, format problems, authorization issues, and repeated timeouts beyond a defined threshold.
The system shall require manual intervention when automatic retry would waste time and hide the real problem.
The system shall keep retrying transient outages for a reasonable window before giving up.
The service should support the official languages relevant to the participating countries.
A machine translation may be sufficient for initial inspection.
If the content is ambiguous, incomplete, or legally sensitive, the system should flag it for human review.
An evidence item may be marked as not applicable only when the criterion genuinely does not apply to the operator or procurement case.
The system shall allow replacement of an evidence item only when the replacement satisfies the same shared requirement and can be mapped back to that requirement.
If there is any doubt about whether to exclude an evidence item, the service should include the item or flag it for review instead of silently dropping it.
If the certificate or attestation still cannot be obtained in time, the case should be escalated for manual follow-up.
An alternative proof may be accepted only if the competent authority has pre-approved that substitute for the same requirement.
Otherwise, the service should wait for the competent authority to decide.
The system shall show a clear exclusion reason such as not applicable to the operator, not required for this opportunity, or replaced by an approved equivalent.
The exclusion explanation shall be visible to audit users or administrators.
If a document contains personal or commercially sensitive data, the system shall sometimes apply extra encryption or provide a redacted view for the receiving side.
If the evidence remains usable for the procurement decision after removing sensitive parts, the system shall prefer redaction.
The system shall record that the item was shared in redacted form and why.
The system shall record the access constraint and protection level when extra encryption is used.
The system shall keep core identifiers stable throughout the dossier or evidence item lifecycle.
The system shall keep the link to the mapped requirement or criterion stable throughout the dossier or evidence item lifecycle.
The system shall update the status when a dossier or evidence item changes state.
The system shall update any package reference when an item is moved into a new package.
Clarification that is only explanatory context and does not change the actual content of a frozen revision shall be captured in a separate annotation layer.
If a clarification would alter the evidence itself, it shall be handled as a new revision or a new submitted document, not as an annotation.
Only the contracting authority, the submitting operator, and authorized auditors shall be able to create or view annotations.
Other project participants or outside counsel should not normally be able to create or view annotations unless they have been explicitly granted case-level access for the dossier.
The authority or operator should be able to grant a limited role through a controlled delegation model.
Any delegated access must be limited to the specific case and must comply with the national rules.
Delegated access should be read-only unless there is a clear business need to annotate.
Any such access must be logged.

If a revision has already been received or referenced in a case, the system shall keep the revision visible and clearly mark it as withdrawn so the history remains intact and reviewers can see what happened.
The withdrawal metadata shall include who withdrew the revision.
Usually only the submitting operator should be allowed to withdraw a revision.
If a revision is already under active review by the authority, withdrawal should require confirmation or approval.
Withdrawal of a revision should be prevented once a decision has been issued on that revision, unless the process allows a formal correction path.
If the authority itself is handling the case, the withdrawal event should be recorded as an action affecting the case history rather than as a normal self-withdrawal.
A withdrawal after a decision on the revision has been issued shall be allowed only in exceptional cases.
A withdrawal after a decision on the revision has been issued shall trigger a formal correction or supersession workflow with approval from the authority.
The original submitter or the delegated operator should normally initiate the withdrawal because they own the evidence package.
The authority must not silently withdraw the submitter’s revision on its own unless the national process explicitly allows it.
If the case is already decided, the correction should usually require logged approval from both the initiating party and the authority handling the dossier.
A pre-approved alternative proof shall be tied to the specific procurement context.
A pre-approved alternative proof that is valid in one country or procedure may not be valid in another.
The system shall show why a pre-approved alternative proof was accepted.
The system shall show who approved the equivalence for a pre-approved alternative proof.
The approver of an accepted equivalence shall be the authority or body that owns the mapping decision, not the operator submitting the dossier.
If the mapping is ambiguous, the system should default to including the evidence item and flagging it for review.
The system should only exclude an evidence item outright when the authority’s rules or the mapping source clearly state that it is out of scope.
If a package cannot be authenticated or opened because of a trust or interoperability failure, the system shall not treat it as a normal successful submission.
If a package cannot be authenticated or opened because of a trust or interoperability failure, the system shall place it into a failed technical handling state first.
When a package enters a failed technical handling state, the authority shall be notified.
If the issue appears temporary, the system shall hold the submission for retry.
If the trust or format problem is persistent, the system shall reject the submission and route it to an alternative manual handling path so the case does not disappear without trace.
The current record for a dossier should be the latest revision that has been accepted as valid and has not been withdrawn or superseded.

A newer revision should supersede the previous revision when it has been successfully submitted, validated, and either explicitly accepted or issued as the replacement version under the workflow rules.
If a newer revision is only a draft, has failed validation, or is marked as supplementary rather than replacing the earlier dossier, the earlier version should remain active.
A temporary technical failure shall be defined as a failure whose underlying cause is clearly transient.
A timeout shall be treated as an example of a temporary technical failure.
A short-lived service outage shall be treated as an example of a temporary technical failure.
An expired connection that can be refreshed automatically shall be treated as an example of a temporary technical failure.
A failure that repeats after a small number of retries shall be treated as persistent.
An error indicating an untrusted certificate shall be treated as persistent.
An unsupported format shall be treated as persistent.
Broken package integrity shall be treated as persistent.
A persistent failure shall cause the package to be rejected from the automated path and sent to manual handling.
The failure reason shall be recorded when a package is sent to manual handling.
